active_invariants: Do not compare naked strings; compare typed transformations.
Carrier is not reading; reading is not language; language is not semantic address.
Sign arity, phonological load, root arity, morphology and semantic compression are independent coordinates.
Spectral precedence is not chronological precedence without independent evidence.
Convergent projections can constrain a hidden state without identifying the hidden substrate.
Material medium is not encoding granularity.
Prefer homology of transformation over identity of surface form.
Parallax depth describes representation distance, not confidence.
Explicit ancient crosswalks outrank retrospective resemblance for calibration.
Name continuity does not imply plot continuity.
Identity carrier, role, episode, and classifier are separate variables.
Decipherment heuristic does not equal final etymology.
Known script does not imply known language.
Externally applied identity may encode observer-relative boundary or jurisdiction rather than ancestry.
Holder, office, function, managed domain and manual task are separate coordinates.
Speaking-name semantics do not by themselves establish historical etymology.
Origin-attribution recurrence does not require literal-person or ancestry continuity.
Carrier-window similarity permits inquiry only under independently licensed transformations.
Ancient office names may be translated by regalia, function, or cult relation while preserving institutional address.
Divine and human role labels can recurse across authority levels without implying entity identity.
A name may predate the narrative role later concentrated around it.
Same entity may acquire a new local sacral/royal name under changed jurisdiction while preserving the older personal carrier.
Strong cross-script name identity does not require secure etymological decomposition.
Surface SA/SAR can be a receiving-language output from more complex onsets such as SF-/SP-.
Same ethnonym can compress diachronically from SAURO- to SAR- without requiring a different population.
Phonemic carrier enrichment at liminal/crossing nodes is a testable candidate pattern, not a universal prefix claim.
Outsider/guest, friend, citizen and sage can be different relational projections of the same person.
Knowledge authority and decision authority are separable coordinates.
Legal/persona recoding can preserve a message while changing its admissible social channel.
Foreign names may receive Greek phonemic resegmentation without establishing historical etymology.
Same-referent multilingual and local epigraphic evidence should outrank isolated receiving-language resemblance for historical carrier reconstruction.
A transmitted Greek phonemic reading can remain valuable reception evidence even when historical backprojection favors a different carrier.
Greek Neilos -> Latin Nilus and Greek Kanobos/Kanopos -> Latin Canopus are same-referent carrier controls.
Relocation and renaming can form one ancient identity transform without implying a universal phonological law.
Repeatedly unfinished literary realizations can preserve a tradition when oral, written, genealogical and archival carriers overlap.
Plato's Critias explicitly distinguishes semantic name translation from phonetic transliteration in the Atlantis transmission.
Ancient geographers explicitly recognized substantial receiving-language reshaping of foreign names.
Textual variants should be tested against related toponyms, hydronyms, geography and independent witnesses.
Prestige names may migrate to new geographies independently of the original referent.
Macro-ethnographic labels can cover many mutually unintelligible local groups.
Titles can persist after the constitution or office structure that produced them has changed.
